To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) the restricted mean survival function is a simple, general measure of the difference between two treatment arms; (b) it can be used to summarize the results of RCTs with time to event outcomes in which the PH assumption is not satisfied; and (c) it can be estimated with good precision by a simple, general method.

(1) the restricted mean survival is a useful general measure for comparing two survival curves; (2) it can be estimated from the Kaplan Meier curve, or by fitting a flexible parametric survival model; (3) the latter approach allows for non PH and can be used for the analysis of the IPASS trial.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
in the presence of non PH, the hazard ratio may be misleading and the restricted mean survival may be a useful alternative.

the restricted mean survival at a fixed time point is a simple and robust measure of treatment effectiveness, which is easy to understand and to interpret and which is valid in the presence of non PH.
in the presence of non PH the hazard ratio should not be used as an estimate of treatment effectiveness.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, in the absence of evidence of PH, the restricted mean survival at a fixed time point, together with its confidence interval, is a useful and valid summary measure of the treatment effect, and it is a simple and robust alternative to the hazard ratio.
the use of the hazard ratio as the primary measure of treatment effect should not be regarded as the gold standard.
, if PH is in doubt, the use of the hazard ratio as a measure of treatment effect should be avoided.
